text.p: Italian debt markets skidded lower in late trade after comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan warning the Fed could not rule out a pre-emptive tightening in monetary policy.
"The BTps were already weak and that made it worse," one broker at London-based brokerage said.

"It's been a strange day," another broker at a London bank said. "In fact it's a bit of a mess with the cash market not moving much but people rolling over positions and closing out basis positions." The November 2006 Btp was 24 basis points down at 103.96 and the most traded July 2006 Btp off 14 at 109.47.
The November Btp was yielding 7.29 percent and the spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund was 170 basis points.
The March future on LIFFE was 36 basis points down at 130.18 and brokers said the market was trading in a broad range of 129.50 to 131.50.
"One day it goes up and everyone gets excited and one day it goes and everyone gets depressed," one broker commented.

"I think it's pretty much going to stay at these levels until EMU prospects area clearer or we have more information on Italy's mini-budget," he added. He noted support at 130.05 had held but added: "If the others start going down we'll follow."

On the home front, brokers' expectations for an Italian interest rate cut were retreating into the second quarter of the year as the lira continued to trade beyond its 990 central parity against the mark.
"And politically there's still a bit of confusion as to whether the government is going to make overtures to the centre right or remain loyal to the hard left," the bank broker said.
"Although up to now the market has trusted the government with having the far left on the inside, maybe it doesn't like so much that more reforms aren't yet going ahead," he said.
